BiblicalUsage: Praise, in Daniel's Aramaic, is given to the right God and to the wrong ones, and the book makes sure we see the difference. Daniel praises the God of his fathers who made the secret known, and Nebuchadnezzar, his understanding returned, praises and honours Him that lives for ever. But at Belshazzar's feast they drank wine and praised the gods of gold and silver, and the same word is used for the praise that damned them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe praise always lands somewhere, and the question is only where. I hold that the praise Daniel and Nebuchadnezzar finally gave belongs to the living God alone, and every other god praised is an idol.
